note: Machine-referenceable layer over docs/adr/** + docs/invariants.md. HUMAN-AUTHORED, hand-maintained (NOT generated). Each entry references an ADR/invariant and lists the enforceable fields a router/context bundle needs; it never restates the ADR prose. Source hierarchy unchanged: source/migrations/tests/config outrank this, this outranks generated knowledge. Update this file when an ADR/invariant changes.

decisions.decision: Conflict resolution order: migrations+apps+tests > schema.ts > bridges(provenance) > AST > communities/INFERRED > docs > memory.
forbidden_changes: treating generated graph facts as authoritative over source/migrations/tests
weakening a test to make code pass instead of fixing the code

decisions.decision: The 4 Class-C tables are INTENTIONAL raw-SQL exceptions and MUST stay raw-SQL-only.
forbidden_changes: modeling any Class-C table as a Drizzle entity

decisions.decision: Raw-SQL runtime MUST be preserved; MUST NOT convert DatabaseService.query/transaction to the Drizzle query builder; never run push/generate/migrate.
forbidden_changes: converting raw SQL to Drizzle query builder

decisions.decision: Query-shaped/partial/domain row types MUST NOT be force-replaced by $inferSelect; replace only when structurally equivalent AND tests prove it.
forbidden_changes: replacing RouterRow/WireguardPeerRecord-style types with $inferSelect without equivalence proof

decisions.decision: Money and byte-quota columns use bigint({mode:'number'}); new such columns follow suit.
forbidden_changes: representing money/byte columns as float or string

decisions.decision: telegram_users.telegram_id is an intentional natural text PK and is NOT a FK to customer_accounts; the join is a soft lookup.
forbidden_changes: inferring this FK from the name collision

decisions.decision: knowledge/** and graphify-out/** are GENERATED and MUST NOT be hand-edited; change the generator and regenerate.
forbidden_changes: hand-editing any file under knowledge/ or graphify-out/

decisions.decision: outbounds.subscription_key is a non-security identity/de-dup hash (SHA-1, truncated); the CodeQL js/weak-cryptographic-algorithm finding (#8) is risk-accepted, not fixed. Any future change to SHA-256 MUST be a human-approved migration with recompute+backfill and atomic cutover (never a naive algorithm swap, which churns every child row).
forbidden_changes: swapping the subscription_key hash algorithm in place without a recompute+backfill migration
treating subscription_key as a security token / exposing it to clients / authorizing off it
